Pompey.fact: Gnaeus Pompeius Magnus (Latin: [ˈŋnae̯.ʊs pɔmˈpɛjjʊs ˈmaŋnʊs]; 29 September 106 BC – 28 September 48 BC), known in English as Pompey ( POM-pee) or Pompey the Great, was a Roman general and statesman who was prominent in the final decades of the Roman Republic. A member of the senatorial nobility, Pompey entered into a military career at an early age.

Pompey.subject: Ancient India
Pompey.question: As a young man, he was a partisan and protégé of the dictator _____, after whose death he achieved significant military and political success
Pompey.fact: As a young man, he was a partisan and protégé of the dictator Sulla, after whose death he achieved significant military and political success. He rose to prominence serving Sulla as a commander during the civil war of 83–81 BC.

Pompey.subject: Ancient India
Pompey.question: He rose to prominence serving _____ as a commander during the civil war of 83–81 BC
Pompey.fact: As a young man, he was a partisan and protégé of the dictator Sulla, after whose death he achieved significant military and political success. He rose to prominence serving Sulla as a commander during the civil war of 83–81 BC.

Pompey.subject: Ancient India
Pompey.question: He celebrated three triumphs and served as a commander in the Sertorian War, the _____, the Third Mithridatic War, and in various other military campaigns
Pompey.fact: He celebrated three triumphs and served as a commander in the Sertorian War, the Third Servile War, the Third Mithridatic War, and in various other military campaigns.

Pompey.subject: Ancient India
Pompey.question: Strabo died in 87 BC during the short-lived civil war known as the _____, although sources differ on whether he succumbed to disease or was murdered by his own soldiers
Pompey.fact: Strabo died in 87 BC during the short-lived civil war called the Bellum Octavianum, although sources differ on whether he succumbed to disease or was murdered by his own soldiers.

Pompey.subject: Ancient India
Pompey.question: He was acquitted, supposedly after agreeing to marry the judge's daughter, _____
Pompey.fact: He was acquitted, supposedly after agreeing to marry the judge's daughter, Antistia.

Pompey.subject: Ancient India
Pompey.question: One of the main issues at stake in 87 BC was the appointment of the consul Sulla as commander of the Roman army in the ongoing _____, an opportunity to amass enormous wealth
Pompey.fact: One of the main issues at stake in 87 BC was the appointment of the consul Sulla as commander of the Roman army in the ongoing First Mithridatic War, an opportunity to amass enormous wealth.

Pompey.subject: Ancient India
Pompey.question: During his absence in the East, his political rivals led by _____, Gnaeus Papirius Carbo and Gaius Marius the Younger regained control of the Roman Senate
Pompey.fact: During his absence in the East, his political rivals led by Lucius Cornelius Cinna, Gnaeus Papirius Carbo and Gaius Marius the Younger regained control of the Roman Senate.

Pompey.subject: Ancient India
Pompey.question: In the spring of 83, Sulla landed in _____
Pompey.fact: In the spring of 83, Sulla landed in Brundisium.

Pompey.subject: Ancient India
Pompey.question: He was greeted by _____ with the title imperator (an appellation meaning "victorious general")
Pompey.fact: Soon after Pompey arrived at Sulla's camp. He was greeted by Sulla with the title imperator (an appellation meaning "victorious general").

Pompey.subject: Ancient India
Pompey.question: Some time later, _____ defeated Gaius Marcius Censorinus, another of Carbo's lieutenants
Pompey.fact: During this campaign Pompey acted as Metellus's cavalry commander. Metellus and Pompey defeated Carbo's lieutenant, the praetor Gaius Carrinas, in a six-hour battle at the river Aesis, only to be blockaded by Carbo himself.

Pompey.subject: Ancient India
Pompey.question: At the end of the campaigning season of 82, the government forces made one final effort to march to the relief of _____
Pompey.fact: Not long afterwards, Pompey successfully ambushed another large force under Censorinus, which was trying to get through to Praeneste where Carbo's consular colleague, Marius the Younger (who was the figurehead of the struggle against Sulla), was blockaded. At the end of the campaigning season of 82, the government forces made one final effort to march to the relief of Praeneste.

Pompey.subject: Ancient India
Pompey.question: They mustered 10,000 legionaries and marched to join forces with the _____ and the Lucanians, fierce enemies of Sulla, who had campaigned against them in the Social War
Pompey.fact: They mustered 10,000 legionaries and marched to join forces with the Samnites and the Lucanians, fierce enemies of Sulla, who had campaigned against them in the Social War.

Pompey.subject: Ancient India
Pompey.question: Unable to break through Sulla's blockade, they marched for undefended Rome, only to be caught just in time and defeated by Sulla at the Battle of the _____
Pompey.fact: Unable to break through Sulla's blockade, they marched for undefended Rome, only to be caught just in time and defeated by Sulla at the Battle of the Colline Gate.

Pompey.subject: Ancient India
Pompey.question: By the end of 82 BC, Sulla had expelled his opponents from Italy and had himself made dictator by passage of an enabling law, the lex _____
Pompey.fact: By the end of 82 BC, Sulla had expelled his opponents from Italy and had himself made dictator by passage of an enabling law, the lex Valeria.

Pompey.subject: Ancient India
Pompey.question: They were supported by a fleet under Carbo, while _____ occupied the Roman province of Africa
Pompey.fact: They were supported by a fleet under Carbo, while Gnaeus Domitius Ahenobarbus occupied the Roman province of Africa.

Pompey.subject: Ancient India
Pompey.question: He restored the deposed _____ to the Numidian throne
Pompey.fact: He restored the deposed Hiempsal to the Numidian throne.

Pompey.subject: Ancient India
Pompey.question: Around this time, his troops began referring to him as Magnus, or "the Great", after _____ the Great, a figure much admired by the Romans
Pompey.fact: Around this time, his troops began referring to him as Magnus, or "the Great", after Alexander the Great, a figure much admired by the Romans.

Pompey.subject: Ancient India
Pompey.question: On returning to _____, he asked for a triumph to celebrate his victories, an unprecedented demand for someone so young
Pompey.fact: On returning to Rome, he asked for a triumph to celebrate his victories, an unprecedented demand for someone so young.

Pompey.subject: Ancient India
Pompey.question: When Sulla died in 78 BC, _____ sought to block his state funeral and roll back some of Sulla's laws, then became proconsul of Cisalpine and Transalpine Gaul in January 77 BC
Pompey.fact: Pompey supported Marcus Aemilius Lepidus as consul for 78 BC; Plutarch claims he did so against Sulla's advice, but some modern historians reject the idea. When Sulla died in 78 BC, Lepidus sought to block his state funeral and roll back some of Sulla's laws, then became proconsul of Cisalpine and Transalpine Gaul in January 77 BC.

Pompey.subject: Ancient India
Pompey.question: When the _____ ordered him back to Rome, Lepidus refused to comply unless granted another term as consul, a proposal that was rapidly rejected
Pompey.fact: When the Senate ordered him back to Rome, Lepidus refused to comply unless granted another term as consul, a proposal that was rapidly rejected. Assembling an army, he began marching on Rome; the Senate responded with a series of measures, one of which was to appoint Pompey to a military command.

Pompey.subject: Ancient India
Pompey.question: Lepidus and the remnants of his army retreated to _____, where he died
Pompey.fact: Lepidus and the remnants of his army retreated to Sardinia, where he died.

Pompey.subject: Ancient India
Pompey.question: Supported by local _____ tribes, he took control of Hispania Ulterior and repeatedly defeated Quintus Caecilius Metellus Pius through skillful use of guerrilla warfare
Pompey.fact: Supported by local Iberian tribes, he took control of Hispania Ulterior and repeatedly defeated Quintus Caecilius Metellus Pius through skillful use of guerrilla warfare.

Pompey.subject: Ancient India
Pompey.question: Sertorius defeated other Roman generals sent to oust him and soon conquered _____ as well
Pompey.fact: Sertorius defeated other Roman generals sent to oust him and soon conquered Hispania Citerior as well.

Pompey.subject: Ancient India
Pompey.question: En route to _____, he subdued a rebellion in Gallia Narbonensis, after which his army entered winter quarters near Narbo Martius
Pompey.fact: En route to Hispania, he subdued a rebellion in Gallia Narbonensis, after which his army entered winter quarters near Narbo Martius.

Pompey.subject: Ancient India
Pompey.question: In early 76 BC, he crossed the Col de Portet and entered the _____ peninsula, where he would remain for the next five years
Pompey.fact: In early 76 BC, he crossed the Col de Portet and entered the Iberian peninsula, where he would remain for the next five years.

Pompey.subject: Ancient India
Pompey.question: Sertorius himself suffered 3,000 casualties, one of whom was _____
Pompey.fact: When Sertorius took over operations against Pompey, Metellus defeated his deputy Lucius Hirtuleius at the Battle of Italica. Sertorius himself suffered 3,000 casualties, one of whom was Hirtuleius.

Pompey.subject: Ancient India
Pompey.question: Once this was ready, he escaped from _____ and used it to disrupt Roman logistics on land and by sea
Pompey.fact: Although Metellus defeated Perperna in a separate battle, Sertorius was able to withdraw to Clunia late in the year, where he repaired the walls to lure his opponents into a siege, while forming garrisons from other towns into a new field army. Once this was ready, he escaped from Clunia and used it to disrupt Roman logistics on land and by sea.

Pompey.subject: Ancient India
Pompey.question: Reinforced by two more legions, in 74 BC he and _____ began a war of attrition against their enemy
Pompey.fact: Lack of supplies forced Metellus to quarter his troops in Gaul, while Pompey wintered among the Vaccaei. Dire straits caused by this stretch of the campaign and Sertorius' guerrilla warfare led Pompey to write a letter to the Senate asking for funds and men, and scolding their lack of support for him and Metellus.

Pompey.subject: Ancient India
Pompey.question: By now, _____ was being undermined by internal divisions
Pompey.fact: As his chief opponent had lost most of his Roman legionaries and could no longer match him in the field, Pompey, along with Metellus, gained the upper hand, conquering more and more Sertorian cities, slowly grinding down Sertorius' revolt. By now, Sertorius was being undermined by internal divisions.

Pompey.subject: Ancient India
Pompey.question: His claim to have ended the war by doing so was a long-standing source of resentment for _____
Pompey.fact: Pompey returned to Italy just before Crassus defeated the main rebel army in 71 BC, arriving in time to massacre 6,000 fugitives from the battle. His claim to have ended the war by doing so was a long-standing source of resentment for Crassus.

Pompey.subject: Ancient India
Pompey.question: Since he was both too young and technically ineligible according to the minimum ages for offices set in place by Sulla in the _____, this required a special senatorial decree
Pompey.fact: Since he was both too young and technically ineligible according to the minimum ages for offices set in place by Sulla in the Lex Cornelia Annalis, this required a special senatorial decree.

Pompey.subject: Ancient India
Pompey.question: One of the most significant was the ability to veto _____ bills, an act often seen as a turning point in the politics of the late Republic
Pompey.fact: Since he was both too young and technically ineligible according to the minimum ages for offices set in place by Sulla in the Lex Cornelia Annalis, this required a special senatorial decree. One of the most significant was the ability to veto Senatorial bills, an act often seen as a turning point in the politics of the late Republic.

Pompey.subject: Ancient India
Pompey.question: Although popular with the people, the measure must have been opposed by the optimates, and thus passing it required support from both consuls, although most extant sources barely mention _____
Pompey.fact: Plutarch suggests Pompey supported Crassus as his co-consul to put him under an obligation. Although popular with the people, the measure must have been opposed by the optimates, and thus passing it required support from both consuls, although most extant sources barely mention Crassus.

Pompey.subject: Ancient India
Pompey.question: Their power and range had increased over the past fifty years, partly because of the decline of traditional naval powers like _____, while previous attempts to subdue them had been unsuccessful
Pompey.fact: Their power and range had increased over the past fifty years, partly because of the decline of traditional naval powers like Rhodes, while previous attempts to subdue them had been unsuccessful.

Pompey.subject: Ancient India
Pompey.question: However, _____ routinely referred to their opponents as "pirates" or "brigands", and some historians argue it is more accurate to see them as a conventional enemy, rather than disorganised outlaws
Pompey.fact: However, Romans routinely referred to their opponents as "pirates" or "brigands", and some historians argue it is more accurate to see them as a conventional enemy, rather than disorganised outlaws.

Pompey.subject: Ancient India
Pompey.question: Principally based in _____, in 68 BC, they raided as far as Ostia, Rome's port, and kidnapped two senators, to general outrage
Pompey.fact: Principally based in Cilicia, in 68 BC, they raided as far as Ostia, Rome's port, and kidnapped two senators, to general outrage.

Pompey.subject: Ancient India
Pompey.question: It granted him proconsular authority for three years in any province within 50 miles of the _____, along with the power to appoint legates and significant financial resources
Pompey.fact: It granted him proconsular authority for three years in any province within 50 miles of the Mediterranean, along with the power to appoint legates and significant financial resources. Pompey spread his forces throughout the Mediterranean to prevent the pirates from escaping a Roman fleet by moving elsewhere.

Pompey.subject: Ancient India
Pompey.question: Concerned by one man holding such wide-ranging powers, the _____ opposed the law, but it was passed by the people
Pompey.fact: Concerned by one man holding such wide-ranging powers, the Senate opposed the law, but it was passed by the people.

Pompey.subject: Ancient India
Pompey.question: Fifteen legates were given specific areas to patrol, while he secured the grain route to _____
Pompey.fact: Fifteen legates were given specific areas to patrol, while he secured the grain route to Rome.

Pompey.subject: Ancient India
Pompey.question: These measures won him control of the western _____ in just 40 days, after which his fleets moved to the east, forcing the pirates back to their bases in Cilicia
Pompey.fact: Pompey spread his forces throughout the Mediterranean to prevent the pirates from escaping a Roman fleet by moving elsewhere. These measures won him control of the western Mediterranean in just 40 days, after which his fleets moved to the east, forcing the pirates back to their bases in Cilicia.

Pompey.subject: Ancient India
Pompey.question: They were granted lands in cities devastated during the _____, notably Soli, renamed Pompeiopolis, and Dyme in Greece, with others sent to towns in Libya and Calabria
Pompey.fact: They were granted lands in cities devastated during the Mithridatic War, notably Soli, renamed Pompeiopolis, and Dyme in Greece, with others sent to towns in Libya and Calabria.

Pompey.subject: Ancient India
Pompey.question: The war began in 74 BC, when the last ruler of _____ died and left his kingdom to Rome, sparking an invasion by Mithridates VI of Pontus, and Tigranes the Great of Armenia
Pompey.fact: The war began in 74 BC, when the last ruler of Bithynia died and left his kingdom to Rome, sparking an invasion by Mithridates VI of Pontus, and Tigranes the Great of Armenia. In 68 BC, Quintus Marcius Rex replaced Lucullus in Cilicia, while Manius Acilius Glabrio received Bithynia.

Pompey.subject: Ancient India
Pompey.question: Lucullus was a skilled general who won numerous victories, but claims he was prolonging the war for "power and wealth" led to a _____ investigation
Pompey.fact: Lucullus was a skilled general who won numerous victories, but claims he was prolonging the war for "power and wealth" led to a Senate investigation.

Pompey.subject: Ancient India
Pompey.question: In 68 BC, _____ replaced Lucullus in Cilicia, while Manius Acilius Glabrio received Bithynia
Pompey.fact: In 68 BC, Quintus Marcius Rex replaced Lucullus in Cilicia, while Manius Acilius Glabrio received Bithynia.

Pompey.subject: Ancient India
Pompey.question: He also assumed leadership of the war against _____, but failed to respond decisively when the latter reoccupied much of Pontus in 67 BC, then attacked Cappadocia, a Roman ally
Pompey.fact: He also assumed leadership of the war against Mithridates, but failed to respond decisively when the latter reoccupied much of Pontus in 67 BC, then attacked Cappadocia, a Roman ally. Seeing an opportunity, in 66 BC Pompey used the tribunate to pass the lex Manilia, giving him extensive powers throughout Asia Minor in order to defeat Mithridates, in addition to those granted by the lex Gabinia.

Pompey.subject: Ancient India
Pompey.question: According to contemporary sources, _____ and a small contingent escaped the battle, outstripped their pursuers, and reached Colchis on the Black Sea
Pompey.fact: When Mithridates offered a truce, Lucullus argued the war was over, but Pompey demanded concessions that could not be accepted. Outnumbered, Mithridates withdrew into Armenia, followed by Pompey, who defeated him at Lycus near the end of 66 BC.

Pompey.subject: Ancient India
Pompey.question: While there, he took control of the _____ from its Roman-backed ruler, his son Machares, who later committed suicide
Pompey.fact: While there, he took control of the Cimmerian Bosporus from its Roman-backed ruler, his son Machares, who later committed suicide.

Pompey.subject: Ancient India
Pompey.question: After winning a series of battles, he reached Phasis and linked up with _____, admiral of his Euxine fleet, before a fresh revolt in Caucasian Albania forced him to retrace his steps
Pompey.fact: After winning a series of battles, he reached Phasis and linked up with Servilius, admiral of his Euxine fleet, before a fresh revolt in Caucasian Albania forced him to retrace his steps.

Pompey.subject: Ancient India
Pompey.question: Victory at the Abas enabled him to impose terms on the _____ and agree truces with other tribes on the northern side of the Caucasus
Pompey.fact: Victory at the Abas enabled him to impose terms on the Albanians and agree truces with other tribes on the northern side of the Caucasus.

Pompey.subject: Ancient India
Pompey.question: In the process, he acquired large amounts of money and prestige, as well as criticism from his opponents in _____, who argued that doing so exceeded his authority
Pompey.fact: In the process, he acquired large amounts of money and prestige, as well as criticism from his opponents in Rome, who argued that doing so exceeded his authority. Pharnaces sent his embalmed body to Pompey, in return for which he was granted the Bosporan Kingdom and made an ally of Rome.

Pompey.subject: Ancient India
Pompey.question: Meanwhile, an ageing _____ had been cornered in Panticapaeum by another of his sons, Pharnaces II of Pontus
Pompey.fact: Relying on his naval blockade to wear down Mithridates, Pompey spent 64 BC annexing the independent and wealthy cities of Syria, which were incorporated into a new Roman province. Meanwhile, an ageing Mithridates had been cornered in Panticapaeum by another of his sons, Pharnaces II of Pontus.

Pompey.subject: Ancient India
Pompey.question: He marched as far as _____, where Aristobulus met him again and promised payment and entry into the kingdom's capital, Jerusalem; however, his supporters refused to admit the Romans
Pompey.fact: He marched as far as Jericho, where Aristobulus met him again and promised payment and entry into the kingdom's capital, Jerusalem; however, his supporters refused to admit the Romans.

Pompey.subject: Ancient India
Pompey.question: Nevertheless, he did not touch its treasures and ordered the _____ to be cleansed and regular worship to resume the following day
Pompey.fact: Hyrcanus's supporters opened the gates, and Aristobulus's faction withdrew to the Temple Mount. Upon capturing the Jerusalem Temple, Pompey entered the Holy of Holies, an act regarded as a desecration, since only the high priest was permitted to enter, and only once each year.

Pompey.subject: Ancient India
Pompey.question: Other organisational changes included creating the province of _____ and Pontus, with the rest of Mithridates' territories distributed among Roman allies
Pompey.fact: Other organisational changes included creating the province of Bithynia and Pontus, with the rest of Mithridates' territories distributed among Roman allies.

Pompey.subject: Ancient India
Pompey.question: Finally, _____ received the coastal region of Pamphylia, previously a centre of piracy, along with other inland areas, and was reorganised into six parts.
Pompey.fact: Finally, Cilicia received the coastal region of Pamphylia, previously a centre of piracy, along with other inland areas, and was reorganised into six parts.

Pompey.subject: Ancient India
Pompey.question: He was awarded a third triumph for his achievements in _____, celebrated on his 45th birthday in 61 BC
Pompey.fact: He was awarded a third triumph for his achievements in Asia Minor, celebrated on his 45th birthday in 61 BC.

Pompey.subject: Ancient India
Pompey.question: A similar measure had been rejected in 63 BC, which arguably made the _____ overconfident in their ability to control popular unrest
Pompey.fact: However, the Senate then refused to ratify the treaties agreed by Pompey as part of his settlement of the East. A similar measure had been rejected in 63 BC, which arguably made the Senate overconfident in their ability to control popular unrest.

Pompey.subject: Ancient India
Pompey.question: With additional support from _____, Caesar became one of the two consuls for 59 BC, the other being the optimate Marcus Calpurnius Bibulus
Pompey.fact: With additional support from Crassus, Caesar became one of the two consuls for 59 BC, the other being the optimate Marcus Calpurnius Bibulus. This meant Caesar could help pass legislation sponsored by Pompey and Crassus, while it was in his interest to keep them aligned, an important factor given the rivalry between his two patrons.

Pompey.subject: Ancient India
Pompey.question: Despite appearing to be the most junior, Caesar thus became central to the _____, an informal political alliance designed to counter-balance the optimates
Pompey.fact: Despite appearing to be the most junior, Caesar thus became central to the First Triumvirate, an informal political alliance designed to counter-balance the optimates.

Pompey.subject: Ancient India
Pompey.question: He was also assigned _____ after its governor died in office, before leaving Rome to launch the Gallic Wars in 58 BC
Pompey.fact: He was also assigned Gallia Transalpina after its governor died in office, before leaving Rome to launch the Gallic Wars in 58 BC.

Pompey.subject: Ancient India
Pompey.question: Senatorial opposition to the triumvirate was led by Cicero, a long-standing _____ ally
Pompey.fact: Senatorial opposition to the triumvirate was led by Cicero, a long-standing Pompeian ally.

Pompey.subject: Ancient India
Pompey.question: Despite this, the latter supported the populist politician _____ in an attack on Cicero for executing Roman citizens without trial during the Catilinarian conspiracy
Pompey.fact: Despite this, the latter supported the populist politician Publius Clodius Pulcher in an attack on Cicero for executing Roman citizens without trial during the Catilinarian conspiracy.

Pompey.subject: Ancient India
Pompey.question: Once in office, they ensured the passage of a law giving _____ the province of Syria and command of a punitive expedition against Parthia, providing him opportunities for both military glory and loot
Pompey.fact: Although Crassus was a long-standing rival, there are also indications Pompey felt his status as the foremost soldier of the Republic was threatened by Caesar's success in Gaul. With this in mind, Pompey set aside his differences with Crassus to promote their joint candidature as consuls for 55 BC.

Pompey.subject: Ancient India
Pompey.question: Accused of using violence during his consulship in 59 BC, _____ had previously been shielded by his proconsular immunity
Pompey.fact: Seeking to end his alliance with Caesar, the optimate Bibulus proposed Pompey be elected sole consul, an unprecedented act backed by both Cato and the tribunate. Accused of using violence during his consulship in 59 BC, Caesar had previously been shielded by his proconsular immunity.

Pompey.subject: Ancient India
Pompey.question: Both consuls for 50 BC, _____ and Gaius Claudius, were opponents of Caesar, as was Curio, a plebeian tribune
Pompey.fact: Both consuls for 50 BC, Paullus and Gaius Claudius, were opponents of Caesar, as was Curio, a plebeian tribune. They initiated legislation to remove Caesar from his command in Gaul, who allegedly bypassed this by bribing Paullus and Curio.

Pompey.subject: Ancient India
Pompey.question: They initiated legislation to remove _____ from his command in Gaul, who allegedly bypassed this by bribing Paullus and Curio
Pompey.fact: Both consuls for 50 BC, Paullus and Gaius Claudius, were opponents of Caesar, as was Curio, a plebeian tribune. They initiated legislation to remove Caesar from his command in Gaul, who allegedly bypassed this by bribing Paullus and Curio.

Ponnani.subject: Ancient India
Ponnani.question: It serves as the administrative center of the Taluk and _____ of the same name
Ponnani.fact: It serves as the administrative center of the Taluk and Block Panchayat of the same name.

Ponnani.subject: Ancient India
Ponnani.question: As of the _____ Census, the municipality forms a part of Malappuram metropolitan area
Ponnani.fact: It is the seventh-most populated municipality in the state, the second-most populated municipality in the district, and the most densely populated municipality in Malappuram district, having about 3,646 residents per square kilometre as of the year 2011. As of the 2011 Census, the municipality forms a part of Malappuram metropolitan area.

Ponnani.subject: Ancient India
Ponnani.question: The port also served as the military headquarters of the _____ rulers
Ponnani.fact: Ponnani is located 68 km south to Kozhikode city, 48 km southwest to Malappuram city, 91 km northwest to Palakkad city, and 50 km northwest to Thrissur city. In the Middle Ages, under the ambitious Hindu chiefs of Kozhikode (the Samutiris/Zamorins), Ponnani developed as one of the most important centers of Muslim trade - both overseas and domestic - on the Arabian Sea.

Ponnani.subject: Ancient India
Ponnani.question: With the arrival of the _____ explorers in the late - 15th century, the city witnessed several battles between the Admirals of Kozhikode and the Portuguese for the monopoly in the Spice Trade
Ponnani.fact: With the arrival of the Portuguese explorers in the late - 15th century, the city witnessed several battles between the Admirals of Kozhikode and the Portuguese for the monopoly in the Spice Trade. Whenever a formal war was broke out between the Portuguese and the Kozhikode rulers, the Portuguese attacked and plundered, as the opportunity offered, the port of Ponnani.

Ponnani.subject: Ancient India
Ponnani.question: The relentless battles lead to the eventual decline of the settlement, with the exodus of _____ merchants, and the rulers who protected it
Ponnani.fact: The relentless battles lead to the eventual decline of the settlement, with the exodus of Middle Eastern merchants, and the rulers who protected it.

Ponnani.subject: Ancient India
Ponnani.question: When _____ came under the kingdom of the Zamorin of Calicut, the rulers of Perumpadappu fled to Kodungallur, and later they moved to Kochi, where they established the Kingdom of Cochin
Ponnani.fact: The original headquarters of the Perumbadappu Swaroopam, who later became the Kingdom of Cochin, was at Chithrakoodam in Vanneri, Perumpadappu, which is located 10 km south to Puthuponnani, in Ponnani taluk. When Perumpadappu came under the kingdom of the Zamorin of Calicut, the rulers of Perumpadappu fled to Kodungallur, and later they moved to Kochi, where they set up the Kingdom of Cochin.

Ponnani.subject: Ancient India
Ponnani.question: It was the home of the revered _____ family
Ponnani.fact: It was the home of the revered Makhdum family. Prominent members of this Yemeni family of Islamic theologians included Zain-ud-Din Makhdum I (1467 - 1521) and his grandson Zain-ud-Din Makhdum II (1530 - 1581).

Ponnani.subject: Ancient India
Ponnani.question: Prominent members of this Yemeni family of Islamic theologians included Zain-ud-Din Makhdum I (_____ - 1521) and his grandson Zain-ud-Din Makhdum II (1530 - 1581)
Ponnani.fact: Prominent members of this Yemeni family of Islamic theologians included Zain-ud-Din Makhdum I (1467 - 1521) and his grandson Zain-ud-Din Makhdum II (1530 - 1581).

Ponnani.subject: Ancient India
Ponnani.question: Makhdum II is known for his formidable historical chronicle Tuhfat al-_____ ("Glory to the Victory of Mujahidun", c
Ponnani.fact: Makhdum II is known for his formidable historical chronicle Tuhfat al-Mujahidin ("Glory to the Victory of Mujahidun", c.

Ponnani.subject: Ancient India
Ponnani.question: _____), first printed and published in Lisbon
Ponnani.fact: 1583), first printed and published in Lisbon.

The root is reflected as q-d-š (Phoenician 𐤒-𐤃-𐤔‎, Hebrew ק־ד־ש) in Northwest Semitic and as q-d-s (Arabic: ق-د-س) in Central and South Semitic.

Rakhigarhi.subject: Ancient India

Rakhigarhi.fact: Rakhigarhi or Rakhi Garhi is a village and an archaeological site in the Hisar District of the northern Indian state of Haryana, situated about 150 km northwest of Delhi.  It is located in the Ghaggar River plain, some 27 km from the seasonal Ghaggar river, and belonged to the Indus Valley Civilisation, being part of the pre-Harappan (6000?/4600-3300 BC), early Harappan (3300-2600 BC), and the mature phase (2600-1900 BC) of the Indus Valley Civilisation.  It was one of the five largest settlements of the ancient civilisation, with most scholars prior to 2014 reporting it to have been between 80 hectares and 100+ hectares in area, comprising five closely-integrated archaeological mounds as the extent of mature-phase urban habitations.  A sixth mound situated in the vicinity, but outside of this group, represented a distinct older period and was likely a separate settlement, while a seventh mound was a cemetery or burial ground belonging to the mature phase

Other related excavation sites in the area are Mitathal and the smaller site Lohari Ragho, which are still awaiting excavation.  DNA-tests by Shinde et al. Ramanuja.subject: Ancient India
Ramanuja.question: He is one of the most important exponents of the _____ tradition in Hinduism
Ramanuja.fact: Ramanuja ([ɾaːmaːnudʑɐ]; Middle Tamil: Rāmāṉujam; Classical Sanskrit: Rāmānuja; c.  date 1017-1137), also known as Ramanujacharya, was an Indian Hindu philosopher, guru and social reformer.  He is one of the most important exponents of the Sri Vaishnavism tradition in Hinduism.  His philosophical foundations for devotional practice were influential in the Bhakti movement.  Ramanuja's guru was Yādava Prakāśa, a scholar who, traditionally, is said to have belonged to the Advaita Vedānta tradition, but probably was a Bhedabheda scholar.  Sri Vaishnava tradition holds that Ramanuja disagreed with his guru and the non-dualistic Advaita Vedānta, and instead followed in the footsteps of Tamil Alvārs tradition, the scholars Nāthamuni and Yamunāchārya

Ramanuja.subject: Ancient India

His theories assert that there exists a plurality and distinction between Ātman (soul) and Brahman (metaphysical, ultimate reality), while he also affirmed that there is unity of all souls and that the individual soul has the potential to realize identity with the Brahman.  == Early life == Ramanuja was born into a Tamil Brahmin community, in a village called Sriperumbudur (present-day Tamil Nadu) under the Chola Empire. Ramanuja.subject: Ancient India

Ramanuja.fact: == Early life == Ramanuja was born into a Tamil Brahmin community, in a village called Sriperumbudur (present-day Tamil Nadu) under the Chola Empire.  His followers in the Vaishnava tradition wrote hagiographies, some of which were composed centuries after his death, and which the tradition believes "at face value. " The traditional hagiographies of Ramanuja state he was born to mother Kānthimathi and father Asuri Keshava Somayāji, in Sriperumbudur, near modern Chennai, Tamil Nādu.  He is believed to have been born in the month of Chithirai under the star Tiruvadhirai.  They place his life from 1017–1137, yielding a lifespan of 120 years.  However, based on 11th- and 12th-century temple records and regional literature outside the Sri Vaishnava tradition, modern era scholars suggest that Ramanuja might have lived from 1077–1157.  Paul syndor notes that "reconstructing his 'historical life' is nearly impossible," and such efforts as Carman's datings (1077-1157), although "well-reasoned," are speculative and "ultimately unverifiable

Ramanuja.subject: Ancient India
Ramanuja.question: Ārāyirappaṭi _____āprabhāva, on the other hand, represents the Tenkalai biography
Ramanuja.fact: Ramanuja has long enjoyed foremost authority in the Sri Vaishnava tradition.  === Hagiographies === A number of traditional biographies of Ramanuja are known, some written in 12th century, some written centuries later such as 14th and 15th century, whereas some as far as the 17th or 18th century, particularly after the split of the Śrīvaiṣṇava community into the Vadakalais and Teṉkalais, where each community created its own version of Ramanuja's hagiography based on earlier primary writings.  The Muvāyirappaṭi Guruparamparāprabhāva by Brahmatantra Svatantra Jīyar represents the earliest Vadakalai biography, and reflects the Vadakalai view of the succession following Ramanuja.  Ārāyirappaṭi Guruparamparāprabhāva, on the other hand, represents the Tenkalai biography.  Other biographies include the Yatirajavaibhavam by Andhrapurna, who was the direct disciple of Ramanuja.  == Historical background == Ramanuja grew up in the Tamil culture, in a stable society during the rule of the Chola dynasty.  This period was one of pluralistic beliefs, where Vaishnava, Shaiva, Smarta traditions, Buddhism and Jainism thrived together

Ramanuja.subject: Ancient India
Ramanuja.question: But bad news awaited them at _____ and they both learned that Yamunacharya had died
Ramanuja.fact: Yamunacharya, the Vaishnavite acharya and the religious head of the Ranganathasamy temple at Srirangam had been closely following Ramanuja from a very young age.  When it was time to pass on the legacy, the acharya sent Mahapurna, a disciple assisting him in temple affairs, to Kanchi to invite Ramanuja to Srirangam.  When Mahapurna met Ramanuja and informed him of his guru's desire, Ramanuja was overjoyed and they both immediately left for Srirangam.  But bad news awaited them at Srirangam and they both learned that Yamunacharya had died.  Heart-broken, Ramanuja then left for Kanchi and refused to worship Sri Ranganatha for he held him responsible for taking away Yamunacharya from this world.  As for Mahapurna, he began to assist Tiruvaranga Araiyar, the son of Yamunacharya in managing the temple affairs.  But as time passed by, Tiruvaranga Araiyar and other senior members of the Vaishnavite order felt that there was a vacuum after Yamunacharya's demise and that they lacked a person who could interpret the Vedas and Sastras like Yamunacharya

Samudragupta.fact: == Personality == Samudragupta's coins depict him as a man of tall stature and muscular physique.  The Allahabad Pillar inscription presents him as a compassionate ruler, stating that his "mind was engaged in providing relief to the low, the poor, the helpless, and the afflicted".  It also mentions that he reinstated many royal families which had lost their kingdoms, including the kings defeated by him.  At the same time, it states that he maintained strict administration ("Prachanda shasana").  The inscription states that Samudragupta became famous among the learned people because of his poetical works, and earned the epithet "king of poets".  This suggests that he composed some poetical works, but none of these works now survive.  The inscription also boasts that Samudragupta put to shame the celestial musician Tumburu and Narada by his lovely performances of music

This elaborate type of sacrifice, known as *chirotsanna*, included *prateyya* or hymns praising the sacrificer and long-ago kings, performed by lute-players including a Rajanya who sang three self-composed songs.  It is possible that the Asokan pillar, on which the prasasti was engraved, was used as an ornamental post during the sacrifice.  Prayaga (modern-day Allahabad) was the original seat of the Gupta dynasty.  Samudragupta's reign marked a significant revival of Brahmanical religion, which had declined since Emperor Ashoka's promotion of Buddhism.  Samudragupta represents a Hindu response to Ashoka’s Buddhist ideals

Sarnath.fact: According to one history, during the local king's hunting trip, a male deer (buck) offered to sacrifice himself to save the life of a female deer (doe) that the king was aiming to kill.  Impressed, the king then declared his park would thereafter be a deer sanctuary.  According to Sutra 16 of the Mahaparinibbana sutra within the Digha Nikaya, the Buddha named Sarnath as one of four Buddhist pilgrimage sites that devout followers should visit and look upon with samvega or feelings of reverence.  The other three sites named by the Buddha are Lumbini, his birthplace; Bodh Gaya, where he achieved enlightenment; and, Kushinagar, where he attained parinirvana.  Sarnath is located eight kilometres (five miles) northeast of Varanasi near the confluence of the Ganges and the Varuna rivers.  == Etymology == The name Sarnath derives from the Sanskrit word Sāranganātha (or Sārangnāth in Pali), which translates into English as 'Lord of the Deer. Sarnath.subject: Ancient India
Sarnath.question: The reliquary contained a few bones and some pearls, which were subsequently thrown into the _____ river
Sarnath.fact: In what is the first incontrovertible modern reference to the ruins at Sarnath, Jonathan Duncan (a charter member of the Asiatic Society and later Governor of Bombay) described the discovery of a green marble reliquary encased in a sandstone box in the relic chamber of a brick stupa at that location.  The reliquary was discovered in January 1794, during the dismantling of a stupa (referred to by Alexander Cunningham as stupa "K" or the "Jagat Singh stupa", later identified as the Dharmarajika Stupa) by employees of Zamindar Jagat Singh (the dewan of Maharaja Chait Singh, the Raja of Benares).  Duncan published his observations in 1799.  The reliquary contained a few bones and some pearls, which were subsequently thrown into the Ganges river.  The reliquary itself has also disappeared, although the outer sandstone box was replaced in the relic chamber, where it was rediscovered by Cunningham in 1835.  The bricks of the stupa were hauled off and used for the construction of the market in Jagatganj, Varanasi.  Jagat Singh and his crew also removed a large part of the facing of the Dhamek Stupa, and removed several Buddha statues which he retained at his house in Jagatganj

Sarnath.subject: Ancient India
Sarnath.question: He had carefully studied the writings of Faxian and Xuanzang, two _____ monks who travelled extensively throughout northern India in the early 5th and early 7th centuries, respectively
Sarnath.fact: Visiting Sarnath in 1815, he was the first to describe a dedicated exploration of the ruins.  Throughout the early 19th century, amateur archeologists explored and excavated at Sarnath, removing antiquities, and several artists drew sketches of the site (especially of the Dhamek Stupa).  In 1835–1836, a 21-year-old British Army engineer with the Bengal Engineer Group named Alexander Cunningham conducted the first systematic archaeological excavations at Sarnath.  He had carefully studied the writings of Faxian and Xuanzang, two Chinese Buddhist monks who travelled extensively throughout northern India in the early 5th and early 7th centuries, respectively.  Based on their writings and those of Duncan, he conducted some careful measurements and excavations at Sarnath in 1835–1836.  During the course of these excavations, Cunningham discovered and removed many statues from monastery "L" and temple "M", as well as the sandstone box reported by Duncan from the Dharmarajika Stupa.  He presented these items to the Asiatic Society of Bengal, and they are now located in the Indian Museum in Kolkata

Sarnath.subject: Ancient India
Sarnath.question: He also recovered a seated _____ statue from Jagat Singh's house and transcribed its inscription
Sarnath.fact: In 1861, Cunningham became the founder and first Director-General of the Archaeological Survey of India.  In 1851–1852, Markham Kittoe (1808–1853) conducted further excavations at Sarnath.  Kittoe noted the presence of four stupas at Sarnath and excavated a structure he described as a hospital, which was located roughly midway between the Dhamek and Jagat Singh stupas.  He also recovered a seated Buddha statue from Jagat Singh's house and transcribed its inscription.  In his writings, Kittoe speculated that Sarnath was destroyed as a result of a great fire.  Sometime in the mid-19th century, Sarnath was subjected to further depredations, as 48 statues and a tremendous amount of bricks and stones were removed from the historic site to be used in the construction of two bridges over the Varuna River.  A final instance of despoilation occurred around 1898, when many bricks and stones were removed from Sarnath and used as ballast for a narrow-gauge railway that was under construction at that time

The Ashokan pillar erected here was broken during the invasions of the 12th century but many of the pieces remain at the original location.  The pillar was originally surmounted by the Lion Capital of Ashoka, which in turn served as the base of a large 32-spoke sandstone wheel of dharma.  The capital and wheel are on display at the Sarnath Archeological Museum, and they symbolize the modern state of India.
